_note: Per iOS screen (SweepFrames.swift names): its Android status (not-ported, in-progress, parity) and the differences still open. Read by scripts/android_parity.py. DECISIONS.md 2026-11-10.

_android_forced.why: SF Symbols exist only on Apple platforms; Android uses Material Symbols, the matching glyph each time (map, search, eco leaf, photo_camera).
Android has no system material blur for what lies under a view; the grey glass is the ground at 92 percent with the iPhone's 6 percent ink wash.
Android's system back gesture and button close the top sheet or page, as every Android app does.
The location and camera questions are the system's own dialogs.
Google instead of Apple; Sign in with Apple does not exist on Android.
Android's own bars at the top and bottom of the screen.
SF Pro, the iPhone's system face, exists only on Apple platforms; Android's own system face (Roboto) stands in at the same sizes and weights. The brand face Gabarito is the same on both.
The share circle on a tree's card opens Android's share sheet with the same tagged link (utm_campaign=map_card).
The Species chip's list is a system sheet on both phones: SwiftUI's .sheet on the iPhone, Material's modal bottom sheet on Android.
The iPhone asks once whether Apple Maps or Google Maps and remembers it; Android has no Apple Maps, so Take me there opens the walking route in the maps app the phone uses.
The report menu on a tree page is the system's own pop-up menu on both phones: SwiftUI's Menu on the iPhone, Material's dropdown menu on Android.
Android's bottom sheet runs the full width of the screen with its own drag handle; the iPhone's sheet on iOS 26 floats with a margin. Content, sizes and order are the same.

Android's photo picker removes a photograph's location before the app sees it, so a photograph chosen from the library always asks where the tree stands (the iPhone reads it off the photograph). The camera path is the same on both.
The iPhone keeps a copy on the phone and sends it in the background; Android keeps nothing on the phone (hard rule 11), so it sends at once and says so when it did not arrive.

differences: Build 42's Airbnb sheet (LOG.md 2026-11-08: only the count bar at the lowest stop, the tab bar hidden) is decided but not in the iPhone's Swift on main yet; Android follows the Swift and takes it when it lands.
Location refused: the iPhone shows its recovery sheet (PermissionRecovery.swift) before Settings; Android opens the app's settings directly. Not ported yet.
Your own trees (photographed by you, not ours) are not on the Android map or in the Collected shelf yet: Android has no store for them until My trees is ported (session 4).
The snackbar after a bookmark ("Added to Want to visit", Undo) is not ported yet.
First launch reads the 11.5 MB catalogue in about ten seconds on the one-core emulator under a loaded Mac; later launches read a binary snapshot. Not yet measured on a real phone.
Under a searched city the ambassador and Plus boxes (PlaceAsksBox, PlusUnderBox) are not ported yet (sessions 5 and 6).
As map.
As map; the share circle opens Android's share sheet (forced). The card is now TreeCard ported whole (TreeRows.kt), its words in every language.
Recent searches (signed in, kept on the server) are not ported yet.
A town we have no trees in (Apple's MKLocalSearch on the iPhone) is not looked up yet; Android says nothing matches.
The on-screen keyboard shows on Android; the iPhone simulator types from the Mac's keyboard, so its shot has none. Both focus the field.
Your own tree (a tree only you have: its menu to change name, species, age, girth, move the pin, merge, remove, and Share this tree) is not ported: it belongs to My trees (session 4).
Approximate location, Show us where it is: the iPhone opens the pin picker (PlacePin.swift); Android opens the report form with The pin is in the wrong place until the picker is ported.

The city link, the species fact, the Discover more chips and the full-map button open the map on that place, species or tree; the iPhone opens the city, country, species and tree-map pages, not ported yet (session 5).
The snackbar after a bookmark (Added to Want to visit, Undo) is not ported yet (as on the map).
The review prompt after three trees and the tree_opened measurement are not ported (session 8).
Collect: Remove from collected (with Undo) in the collect sheet is not ported yet.
As tree.
Sign-in sheet written from the website's copy; SignIn.swift not ported.
A species (a pill, By species See all, a species search hit) opens the map filtered to that species; the iPhone opens its species page, which is not ported yet.
A visitor's name, signed in, opens their public profile on the website (ancienttrees.app/profile?u=); the iPhone opens PersonProfile, not ported yet. Signed out both ask for a sign-in first.
Want to visit's See all goes to the account sheet's lanes until My trees is ported.
The lists, the oldest trees and the See all pages show their trees as rows (TreeRow), not TreeCard; TreeCard has landed from the tree page and replaces them next.

The ambassador explainer is drawn as its own sheet in Discover.kt; it moves onto BrandSheet.kt (now on main from the tree page). A failed request is a one-line sheet, not the snackbar, until a snackbar is ported.

A card face with no website choice falls back to the first photographed tree; the iPhone's fallback also weighs the photograph's size, which the Android feed reader does not read yet. The feed carries a face for every shelf today, so nothing shows this.
Pull to refresh is Material's spinner, the Android counterpart of the iPhone's refresh control (forced).
My trees (Collect.swift) not ported; the tab opens the account sheet for now.
Profile and settings (Profile.swift) not ported.
Delete photo (for your own photographs) comes with My trees (session 4).
The locate arrow in the corner of the map is not drawn on Android yet.
Your own trees within 30 m (a second photograph of a tree you added) are not offered at the top of the list yet: they come from My trees, which is not ported.
The App Store style review ask two seconds after a new tick is not ported (session 8).
The ⋯ menu on the draft and the add tile under More photographs (a further photograph, the sign) are not ported yet.
The city under the name is not a link yet (the place pages are not ported).
After Save the page closes; on the iPhone it stays as your tree with Share, which needs My trees (not ported).
Ported with Discover (CollectionView in Home.swift): the intro and the trees, as rows (TreeRow) rather than TreeCard until the card from the tree page is swapped in.

_shared._note: Pieces every screen uses. One owner each; a screen session changes them only through its owner.
